sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Fixed numbers for reveal and comparison
sections.what: Sets 10 graded calls as the reveal point, 5 other calls as the minimum to compare a crowd, and 3 calls in each of the middle and death overs before timing is compared.
sections.why: Likely reason: avoids judging a fan on too little data.
sections.watch_out: Changing these numbers changes who gets a profile and when.

sections.name: IdentityCall, PersonaSlug, NAMES, ORDER, Axis
sections.title: Call format and persona names
sections.what: Describes what one graded call contains, and lists the five persona slugs, their display names and their order.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared input format and fixed names for the output.
sections.watch_out: Sport and phase are plain text, so a typo in upstream data would not be caught by the type.

sections.name: Identity, rate, pct, clamp, lc, TYPE_NAME
sections.title: Small helpers and result shape
sections.what: Defines the hidden and revealed result types and small helpers: hit rate, percentage text, keeping numbers between 0 and 1, lowering the first letter of a sentence, and a name map for decision types.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the main function short and the wording consistent.
sections.watch_out: The lowercase helper fails on an empty string.

sections.name: alterEgo (part 1)
sections.title: Working out the five habits
sections.what: Returns hidden if there are fewer than 10 calls. Otherwise measures risk from how often the faster option was backed, timing from the gap between death and middle overs, calibration from confidence against results, contrarianism from going against the crowd, and domain mix from the most common decision type.
sections.why: Likely reason: each habit is plain and explainable, as the product spec asks.
sections.watch_out: Timing and contrarianism have no value when data is thin, so the habit shows no figure rather than zero.

sections.name: alterEgo (part 2)
sections.title: Choosing the persona and explanation
sections.what: Measures clutch play as the gap between hit rate on higher-leverage calls and the rest, scores each persona, picks the top one, falls back to the main sport's persona when no trait stands out, picks a modifier such as Contrarian or Bold, and writes the evidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: the explanation must match the chosen persona so the fan can see why they got it.
sections.watch_out: In a tie, the persona listed first wins, and the sport fallback relies on all scores being zero.

summary: Works out a fan's Alter Ego identity from their graded calls: five habits, then one of five analyst personas and a modifier, once enough calls exist.
purpose: Turns a fan's record into an explainable profile, shown only after a set number of graded calls.
why: The header refers to the Alter Ego product spec. The code is described as deterministic and explainable, so the same calls always give the same profile.
how: Returns hidden until at least 10 graded calls. Works out risk, timing, calibration, contrarianism and domain mix. Scores each persona, picks the highest, falls back to the main sport's persona when no trait stands out, chooses a modifier, and writes evidence sentences.
inputs: A list of graded calls, each with relation to the moment, phase, decision type, sport, confidence, result, leverage and crowd agreement.
outputs: Either hidden with the count of calls left, or revealed with the axes, persona, modifier, label and evidence.
risks: Thresholds are fixed in code, so changing them changes every fan's profile. Timing and contrarianism have no value for small samples.
debug: If a profile looks odd, check the relation, phase and crowd values on that fan's calls. If the sport persona looks wrong, check the sport names, since unknown sports fall back to The Opener.
